LEFT: an enlarged actual OVERHAND LOOP KNOT TIED ON A BIGHT, in a continuous natural twisted cord: a narrow teardrop-shaped fixed terminal eye above a compact doubled-overhand knot, two parallel strands visibly enter the knot, the standing part and short free tail exit below; real over-under crossings and broken hidden-line conventions make the continuous cord traceable. The eye is NOT a detached toroidal rope ring, splice, metal ring or unattached circular object. Label with thin leaders FIXED TERMINAL EYE, DOUBLED OVERHAND KNOT, SHORT TAIL, STANDING PART. RIGHT: the same tied terminal eye with the long standing part returned THROUGH THE OPENING of that eye, forming a larger adjustable loop below. Show the running strand distinctly traversing the eye opening once, with a white separation at the crossing so its path is readable. This larger adjustable loop is a continuation of the SAME cord, not separate rings glued together. A leader RUNNING LINE THROUGH EYE points to that crossing; a leader ADJUSTABLE LOOP points to the large loop. Preserve visible knot and tail, eye elongated and small, large loop loose and irregular. One cord colour, use navy outline and pale ochre fill; a subtle sage arrow may mark the moving strand without disguising rope paths. Keep knot topology faithful to a genuine overhand loop on a bight; no invented interlocking links, no smooth doughnut called a fixed eye. No animal, hand, sapling, spring installation, rope ball or metal component. Crisp legible sparse lettering, ample breathing space, elegant mid-century technical plate.
